title: Console settings: Region pinning (data residency) – wire notes + copy/validation
content:
Working notes for Console settings UX (Region pinning / Hosted data residency enforcement). This doc is intentionally “wire notes” quality: proposed field names, UI layout, inline validation messages, and what we show for recent violations. Audience: Console eng + PM + Security.

Source of truth: Confluence PRD + error code taxonomy + audit event spec (linked above). Console should not invent new policy semantics; just present them cleanly.

---
Meeting(s)
- 2025-01-14: initial wire review (Felix/Nora + Marissa + Naomi)
- 2025-01-28: copy/validation review (Brian + Marcus + Naomi)
- 2025-02-05: “recent violations” panel + RBAC check (Chloe + Felix + Security)

Primary goals for Console surface
1) Allow enterprise admins to configure region pinning quickly and safely (with guardrails).
2) Make residency failures actionable: show what’s wrong (client region vs pinned region), how to fix (base URL / SDK region), and where to get evidence (audit event ID).
3) Make policy “sticky” and explicit: discourage cross-region fallback, require deliberate opt-in + warning if an exception is granted.

Non-goals for Console (v1)
- Migration of existing stored artifacts.
- Deep analytics/exploration (leave for dashboards); Console just shows a small “recent violations” snapshot + linkouts.

---
Terminology (customer-facing)
- Preferred term in UI: “Data residency (region pinning)”
- Avoid: “geo-fencing” (Naomi preference; could be construed as marketing-y)
- Use “region” not “cluster”

---
Where in Console does this live?
Proposed nav:
- Org Settings → Security & Compliance → Data residency
- Also consider surface at Project Settings (if project-level override exists). For v1: show at both, but editing depends on precedence rules.

Important: policy scope/precedence
- We need to show what scope is currently effective.
- If both org + project exist, show “Effective policy: Project override” with a link to project settings.
- If org is set and project is unset, show “Inherited from Org”.

UI block header
- Title: Data residency (region pinning)
- Subtitle: “Restrict request processing and related artifacts to approved regions.”
- “Learn more” link → docs page (final URL TBD; keep as placeholder in early builds)

---
Settings model (as shown in UI)
We have two concepts in backend: pinned_region and allowed_regions.
Console should present this as a simple primary choice with optional advanced controls.

Proposed UI structure:
A) Toggle: “Enforce data residency”
- Off: show neutral state (no region constraints). If org has enterprise tier, consider default On (but that’s rollout/feature flag; UI just reflects current).
- On: show region selection + enforcement behavior.

B) Region selector: “Pinned region” (single-select)
- Copy: “Requests will only be processed in this region. Cross-region fallback is blocked unless an exception is explicitly enabled.”
- Single select dropdown with region labels.

Region label format
- Show canonical region code + friendly name
  - Example: “eu-west (EU West)”
  - Example: “us-east (US East)”
- Add “(Limited availability)” if known constrained capacity regions (optional; might be a future enhancement).

Supported regions list (placeholder)
- us-east
- us-west
- eu-west
- eu-central
(Need to match platform’s actual list; do not hardcode outside shared regions util.)

C) Advanced: “Allowed regions” (multi-select) – only if we truly support it in v1
Recommendation from Naomi/Brian: don’t expose both pinned_region and allowed_regions as first-class controls simultaneously; it confuses the guarantee.

Option 1 (recommended): UI only exposes pinned region; allowed_regions remains internal/future.
Option 2: UI exposes allowed regions only in “Advanced” accordion, read-only unless a feature flag is enabled.

Proposed advanced panel wording (read-only for now):
- Label: “Approved regions (advanced)”
- Helper: “If set, requests must be processed in one of these regions. If a pinned region is also set, the pinned region must be included.”
- If user can’t edit: “Contact support to configure multi-region approval.”

D) Cross-region fallback override (exception path)
We should not call this “fallback” alone; explicitly tie to compliance.
- Control name: “Allow cross-region fallback (exception)” (toggle)
- Default: Off
- Warning callout when toggled On:
  Title: “Compliance exception”
  Body: “Enabling cross-region fallback may result in processing outside the pinned region during capacity events. This should only be enabled under an approved exception process. All cross-region decisions will be audit-logged.”
  Confirmation: require typing “ALLOW” or checking “I understand” (Marissa suggestion).
- Visibility: only for roles with permission + only if backend says exception is permitted.

Naomi note: exceptions must be time-bound in GRC process. Console should show expiry if present.
- Read-only field: “Exception expires” with date/time + “Request extension” link.

---
Field names (API → Console mapping)
We need stable names for the UI forms and event attributes for troubleshooting.

Suggested internal form keys (Console frontend)
- residency.enforcement_enabled (bool)
- residency.pinned_region (string)
- residency.allowed_regions (string[])
- residency.allow_cross_region_fallback (bool)
- residency.exception_expires_at (string, ISO8601)

Display-only “effective” values
- residency.effective_scope: “org” | “project” | “workspace” (if workspace exists)
- residency.effective_pinned_region
- residency.effective_allowed_regions

---
Inline validation + error copy (Console)
We need two classes of errors:
1) Client-side form validation (before save)
2) Server-side policy validation errors (returned by Console API), mapped into friendly messages

Client-side validation (proposed messages)
- If enforcement_enabled = true and pinned_region is empty:
  “Select a pinned region to enable enforcement.”
- If allowed_regions is editable and pinned_region not in allowed_regions:
  “Pinned region must be included in approved regions.”
- If exception toggle is On but pinned region is empty:
  “Set a pinned region before enabling an exception.”

Server-side validation mapping (examples)
- POLICY_INVALID_REGION
  “This region isn’t supported for your plan or deployment. Choose a different region or contact support.”
- POLICY_PINNED_NOT_IN_ALLOWED
  “Pinned region must be included in approved regions.”
- POLICY_SCOPE_CONFLICT
  “A project-level policy overrides this org setting. Edit the project policy to make changes.”

Save button + toasts
- Primary CTA: “Save residency settings”
- Success toast: “Data residency settings updated.”
- Failure toast (generic): “Couldn’t update settings. Review the errors and try again.”

---
How we display “recent violations” in settings
Goal: give admins immediate feedback that something is wrong and how to fix it.

Proposed layout: after settings card, add a panel
Panel title: “Recent residency violations”
Panel subtitle: “Denied requests due to data residency enforcement. See audit logs for full details.”

Table columns (keep minimal)
- Time (relative + hover absolute): “5m ago” / “2025-02-06 14:03:22 UTC”
- Project (name) (if scope=org)
- Endpoint/Route (e.g., /v1/chat.completions)
- Client region / Requested region (if present; from request context) – label it carefully
  - Suggested label: “Request region” (meaning where the request was sent / which regional endpoint)
- Pinned region (effective)
- Error code
- Audit event ID (copy button)

Row click → “Violation details” side panel (not a new page in v1)
Side panel fields
- Error code: RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH (etc.)
- Message: show exact API message (so Support can match)
- Remediation: short steps + docs link
- “Open in Audit Logs” deep link (if we have an audit log explorer)
- Request ID (if safe)
- Org/Project IDs (for support)

Empty state
- If enforcement enabled and no violations in last 24h:
  “No violations detected in the last 24 hours.”
- If enforcement disabled:
  “Enable enforcement to start monitoring residency decisions.” (Note: we may still log decisions even if disabled; confirm.)

Time range selector (optional)
- Default: “Last 24 hours”
- Dropdown: 1h / 24h / 7d
(If not building now, keep fixed at 24h to reduce complexity.)

Data source
- Do NOT query Prometheus/Grafana from Console.
- Prefer query of audit log index / internal events API that backs “Audit logs” explorer.
- Must respect RBAC: users who can change settings can usually view violations; but some orgs may restrict audit log visibility. If user can’t view:
  “You don’t have permission to view violations. Contact an org admin.”

---
Actionable remediation copy (aligned to API error taxonomy)
Console should present 2–3 steps max. Keep consistent with error-codes-data-residency spec.

For RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH
Suggested remediation block:
- Title: “How to fix”
- Steps:
  1. “Send requests to the {pinned_region} endpoint.”
  2. “If you’re using an SDK, set the client region to {pinned_region} (or update your base URL).”
  3. “Confirm your org/project residency settings match your intended deployment.”
- Footnote: “If you believe this denial is unexpected, share Audit event ID {id} with Support.”

For RESIDENCY_FALLBACK_BLOCKED
- “Capacity fallback to another region was blocked by your residency policy.”
- Steps:
  1. “Retry later or reduce concurrency.”
  2. “If you need failover, request a temporary exception (requires approval).”

For RESIDENCY_POLICY_EVALUATION_FAILED (if we have it)
- “We couldn’t evaluate your residency policy. Requests are denied to protect compliance.”
- Steps:
  1. “Retry.”
  2. “If this persists, contact Support and include Request ID.”

---
Console warning banners (when saving a risky change)
Naomi requested we explicitly warn when tightening policies (because it can break production).

Case: turning enforcement On (previously Off)
- Banner (before saving):
  Title: “This may cause request denials”
  Body: “Once enabled, requests sent to other regions will be denied with a residency error. Update your endpoints/SDK config before enabling.”

Case: changing pinned region
- Banner:
  Title: “Changing pinned region will immediately affect traffic”
  Body: “Requests will be denied until clients send traffic to the new region.”

Case: disabling enforcement
- Banner:
  Title: “Disabling enforcement removes residency restrictions”
  Body: “This may affect your compliance posture.”

---
RBAC / permissions
We need two separate permissions (suggested naming; actual controlled by rbac-policy-bundle)
- Manage residency settings (write)
- View residency violations summary (read)

UX behavior
- If user lacks write permission: settings controls read-only, show tooltip “You don’t have permission to edit data residency settings.”
- If user lacks read permission: hide violations panel or show locked state.

---
Edge cases / open questions (to resolve)
1) Dedicated vs Hosted
- Dedicated: region pinning should align with the dedicated region; Console should prevent selecting a pinned region that doesn’t match provisioned capacity.
- Hosted: user can choose among available Hosted regions.

2) Private/VPC deployments
- Likely not applicable in the same way; show “Managed by your private deployment configuration” and link to docs. (Vivek to confirm semantics; keep UI simple.)

3) Multi-region “allowed” without pinned
- If allowed_regions supports multiple regions, what does routing do? Is cross-region fallback permitted within allowed set? (Probably yes.)
- For now, keep pinned as primary; do not encourage multi-region unless product explicitly supports.

4) “Request region” definition
- In violations table, ensure we’re not misleading: request may be sent to “us-east” endpoint but physically originate elsewhere. We should use “Endpoint region” or “Target region”.
- Proposed label: “Endpoint region” (clearer than “Client region”).

5) Severity / alerting
- Console should not show alert thresholds; that’s in Grafana. But could show a simple count: “X violations in last 24h”.

6) Localization readiness
- Brian request: keep copy in i18n-friendly keys (Console already does this); avoid embedding region codes mid-sentence if it complicates translation. (But we do need to interpolate {pinned_region}.)

---
Implementation notes (Console eng)
- Feature flag: keep entire settings page behind residency_enforcement_console (name TBD).
- Settings read/write endpoints should return both configured policy and effective policy (after inheritance + validation).
- For “recent violations”, request an endpoint that supports:
  - org_id, optional project_id
  - time range
  - pagination
  - returns: timestamp, project, route, endpoint_region, pinned_region, error_code, audit_event_id, request_id (optional)

---
Next steps
- Marissa/Felix: confirm what we expose in v1 (pinned only vs allowed advanced).
- Chloe/Nora: wire up locked/read-only states for RBAC.
- Brian: final review of remediation copy against error-codes-data-residency.
- Naomi: confirm exception UI requirements (expiry required? manual vs automated?) and whether Console can display “Exception request” link (process doc).

Notes to self (Felix)
- Keep the UI consistent with how we describe this on sales calls: “no cross-region failover unless explicitly allowed + audit logged.” The Console needs to reinforce that guarantee, not undermine it with ambiguous multi-select controls.
- The violations panel is the fastest way to make Support successful. If we have to cut scope, keep: timestamp + endpoint region + pinned region + error code + audit event ID.
